sources.entry: Trace - Automatic time tracker that records apps, windows, files, and web pages, with all data kept on your Mac. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/lxyeternal/Trace) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Trace is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that automatically tracks which apps, windows, files and web pages you use and for how long, keeping the data on your Mac.
keywords: track how i spend time on my mac
use_cases: see where time goes on a Mac each day
track time per project without timers
tag activity as work, study or entertainment
set daily goals for categories of work
review weekly or monthly productivity reports
sync tracking data across several Macs via iCloud Drive
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL> (the README leaves the URL blank)
Grant Accessibility access in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility
Optional: open -n build/Trace.app --args --demo to see demo data
notable: Automatic tracking with no timers: records the frontmost app, window, file and page, drillable from tag to app to file to page
Projects are inferred from the folder a file sits in (git repo, Swift package, Obsidian vault, or Documents subfolder)
Optional sync via iCloud Drive or any other synced folder, with one file per day per Mac so Macs never edit the same file
Stores only app names and Accessibility-derived titles, paths and URLs; query strings and credentials are stripped from URLs
Demo mode with made-up data for trying the interface without recording
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later; needs Accessibility access for window titles, file paths and URLs
Private browsing windows are not detected; page addresses only for Safari and Chromium-based browsers
With sync on, time is not de-duplicated across Macs used at the same moment
Building from source needs Xcode 16 or later; ad-hoc builds prompt for Accessibility access after every rebuild unless a signing certificate is configured
